literature.headline_zh: 猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期猴痘病毒（Mpox病毒）研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 深度学习图像分类器在诊断文献中占主导地位,其报道的区分 猴痘 皮肤病变与临床模拟的准确度和曲线下面积值范围约为 0.83 至 0.99。时间序列和神经网络模型(ARIMA、LSTM、GRU 和集成亚流行框架)产生了可靠的短期病例预测,而自然语言处理管道则近乎实时地跟踪公众情绪和错误信息。人工智能辅助的 基因组监测、废水监测以及基于结构的药物和表位发现代表了快速新兴但不太成熟的领域。 [10.1186/s12982-026-03038-y]
系统发育分析证实所有泰国分离株均为 Ib 分支,与国际 Ib 分支病毒密切相关,与 Ia 分支参考相比,C3L 基因区域有 1,140 bp 缺失和 52-61 个氨基酸取代。 [10.1128/spectrum.00516-26]
Ib 和 IIb.A.2.1 谱系的感染表明,两种猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 变种都会引起皮肤和睾丸病变,以及鼻腔、皮肤和睾丸组织的病毒排泄。 [10.1080/21505594.2026.2728484]
我们研究了不同的 疫苗接种 策略如何影响分叉方向,并分析了各种初始暴露和感染人群水平的相应吸引盆地。 [10.1038/s41598-026-72308-1]
筛选显示,VACV 诱导的脂质化是双向调节的。 [10.1128/spectrum.01221-26]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Deep-learning image classifiers dominated the diagnostic literature, with reported accuracies and area-under-the-curve values ranging from approximately 0.83 to 0.99 for distinguishing mpox skin lesions from clinical mimics. [10.1186/s12982-026-03038-y]

Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all Thai isolates as clade Ib, showing close relatedness to international clade Ib viruses and exhibiting a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with the clade Ia reference. [10.1128/spectrum.00516-26]
Among the 1,162 reported mpox cases, 776 (66.8%) were from large urban areas. [10.1186/s12982-026-02649-9]

Infection with the Clade Ib and IIb.A.2.1 lineages revealed that both Monkeypox virus (MPXV) variants caused skin and testicular lesions, as well as viral excretion from the nasal cavity, skin, and testicular tissue. [10.1080/21505594.2026.2728484]

We investigate how different vaccination strategies influence the direction of bifurcation and analyze the corresponding basins of attraction for various initial exposed and infected population levels. [10.1038/s41598-026-72308-1]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期猴痘病毒(Mpox病毒)研究集中呈现以下进展。
深度学习图像分类器在诊断文献中占主导地位,其报道的区分 猴痘 皮肤病变与临床模拟的准确度和曲线下面积值范围约为 0.83 至 0.99。时间序列和神经网络模型(ARIMA、LSTM、GRU 和集成亚流行框架)产生了可靠的短期病例预测,而自然语言处理管道则近乎实时地跟踪公众情绪和错误信息。人工智能辅助的 基因组监测、废水监测以及基于结构的药物和表位发现代表了快速新兴但不太成熟的领域。
系统发育分析证实所有泰国分离株均为 Ib 分支,与国际 Ib 分支病毒密切相关,与 Ia 分支参考相比,C3L 基因区域有 1,140 bp 缺失和 52-61 个氨基酸取代。 [10.1128/spectrum.00516-26]。
Ib 和 IIb.A.2.1 谱系的感染表明,两种猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 变种都会引起皮肤和睾丸病变,以及鼻腔、皮肤和睾丸组织的病毒排泄。 [10.1080/21505594.2026.2728484]。
我们研究了不同的 疫苗接种 策略如何影响分叉方向,并分析了各种初始暴露和感染人群水平的相应吸引盆地。 [10.1038/s41598-026-72308-1]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.

Deep-learning image classifiers dominated the diagnostic literature, with reported accuracies and area-under-the-curve values ranging from approximately 0.83 to 0.99 for distinguishing mpox skin lesions from clinical mimics.

Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all Thai isolates as clade Ib, showing close relatedness to international clade Ib viruses and exhibiting a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with the clade Ia reference.

papers.title: Genomic characteristics of the first five monkeypox virus clade Ib cases in Thailand: August 2024–March 2025
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Following the emergence of monkeypox virus clade Ib in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in August 2024, the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern because of sustained transmission and international spread. We characterized the first clade Ib cases detected in Thailand between August 2024 and March 2025 and assessed their phylogenetic relationships. Whole-genome sequencing was performed from lesion swabs of suspected cases. Phylogenetic analysis, incorporating clade Ia ( DQ011155.1 ) and global clade Ib sequences from GISAID, confirmed all Thai isolates as clade Ib. The genomes showed close relatedness to clade Ib viruses reported internationally, consistent with patients’ travel histories. All isolates exhibited a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with the clade Ia reference. Genome sequences were submitted to GISAID and NCBI to support outbreak response and improve understanding of epidemiologic patterns, enabling more effective public health interventions. IMPORTANCE On 14 August 2024, the World Health Organization declared the monkeypox virus outbreak in Africa a public health emergency of international concern following the emergence of clade Ib. One week later, Thailand confirmed the first monkeypox clade Ib case in Asia. Through whole-genome sequencing and phylogenomic analysis of five cases detected between August 2024 and March 2025, we identified a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region that distinguishes clade Ib from clade Ia. This deletion directly affects the performance of some commercial real-time PCR assays designed for clade Ia, which rely on amplification of the missing genomic region. Our findings highlight important diagnostic limitations that could lead to misinterpretation or reduced sensitivity in routine testing. Beyond confirming regional introduction linked to global spread, this study underscores the critical role of genomic surveillance in ensuring accurate diagnosis, monitoring viral evolution, and strengthening outbreak response as monkeypox continues to expand internationally.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to understand the emergence of monkeypox virus clade Ib in Thailand and its implications for public health, as the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern due to sustained transmission and international spread following its emergence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in August 2024.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the first five monkeypox virus clade Ib cases detected in Thailand between August 2024 and March 2025, assessing their phylogenetic relationships with global clade Ib sequences from GISAID and clade Ia reference sequences.
analysis.methods: Whole-genome sequencing was performed from lesion swabs of suspected cases, and phylogenomic analysis was conducted to compare the Thai isolates with clade Ia and global clade Ib sequences, identifying a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and amino acid substitutions.
analysis.main_results: Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all Thai isolates as clade Ib, showing close relatedness to international clade Ib viruses and exhibiting a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with the clade Ia reference.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings confirm the regional introduction of clade Ib monkeypox virus linked to global spread and highlight the importance of genomic surveillance in monitoring viral evolution and improving diagnostic accuracy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights for enhancing diagnostic testing, understanding transmission dynamics, and informing public health interventions as monkeypox continues to spread internationally.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to five cases and relies on genomic data, which may not fully capture the epidemiologic patterns, but the evidence is strong due to the use of global reference sequences and direct sequencing of Thai isolates.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the genomic characteristics of the first five monkeypox virus clade Ib cases in Thailand between August 2024 and March 2025. It confirmed that these isolates belong to clade Ib, showing close relatedness to international clade Ib viruses and exhibiting a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with clade Ia. The research highlights the importance of genomic surveillance in tracking viral evolution and improving diagnostic accuracy, especially as clade Ib continues to spread globally. The study's findings underscore the need for updated diagnostic methods to account for these genetic differences, which affect the performance of some commercial real-time PCR assays. While the study is limited to a small sample size and relies on genomic data, the evidence is strong due to the use of global reference sequences and direct sequencing of the Thai isolates. The results contribute to understanding the epidemiologic patterns of monkeypox and support more effective public health interventions.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to understand the emergence of monkeypox virus clade Ib in Thailand and its implications for public health, as the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern due to sustained transmission and international spread following its emergence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in August 2024.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the first five monkeypox virus clade Ib cases detected in Thailand between August 2024 and March 2025, assessing their phylogenetic relationships with global clade Ib sequences from GISAID and clade Ia reference sequences.
elements_en.methods: Whole-genome sequencing was performed from lesion swabs of suspected cases, and phylogenomic analysis was conducted to compare the Thai isolates with clade Ia and global clade Ib sequences, identifying a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and amino acid substitutions.
elements_en.main_results: Phylogenetic analysis confirmed all Thai isolates as clade Ib, showing close relatedness to international clade Ib viruses and exhibiting a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with the clade Ia reference.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings confirm the regional introduction of clade Ib monkeypox virus linked to global spread and highlight the importance of genomic surveillance in monitoring viral evolution and improving diagnostic accuracy.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides critical insights for enhancing diagnostic testing, understanding transmission dynamics, and informing public health interventions as monkeypox continues to spread internationally.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to five cases and relies on genomic data, which may not fully capture the epidemiologic patterns, but the evidence is strong due to the use of global reference sequences and direct sequencing of Thai isolates.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 需要开展这项研究来了解猴痘病毒 Ib 分支在泰国的出现及其对公共卫生的影响,因为由于 传播 的持续存在以及 2024 年 8 月在刚果民主共和国出现后的国际传播,世界卫生组织宣布该病毒为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了 2024 年 8 月至 2025 年 3 月期间在泰国发现的前 5 例猴痘病毒 Ib 分支病例,评估了它们与 GISAID 的全球 Ib 分支序列和 Ia 分支参考序列的系统发育关系。
elements_zh.methods: 对疑似病例的病变拭子进行全 基因组 测序,并进行系统发育分析,将泰国分离株与 Ia 分支和 Ib 分支序列进行比较,鉴定出 C3L 基因区域的 1,140 bp 缺失和氨基酸替换。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析证实所有泰国分离株均为 Ib 分支,与国际 Ib 分支病毒密切相关,与 Ia 分支参考相比,C3L 基因区域有 1,140 bp 缺失和 52-61 个氨基酸取代。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证实了 Ib 分支猴痘病毒的区域引入与全球传播有关,并强调了 基因组监测 在监测病毒 进化 和提高诊断准确性方面的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 随着猴痘继续在国际上传播,该研究为加强诊断测试、了解 传播 动态以及为公共卫生干预措施提供重要见解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于五个病例,并依赖于基因组数据,这可能无法完全捕捉流行病学模式,但由于使用了全球参考序列和泰国分离株的直接测序,证据是强有力的。

papers.title_zh: 泰国前 5 例猴痘病毒 Ib 分支病例的基因组特征:2024 年 8 月至 2025 年 3 月
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Following the emergence of monkeypox virus clade Ib in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in August 2024, the World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern because of sustained transmission and international spread. We characterized the first clade Ib cases detected in Thailand between August 2024 and March 2025 and assessed their phylogenetic relationships. Whole-genome sequencing was performed from lesion swabs of suspected cases. Phylogenetic analysis, incorporating clade Ia ( DQ011155.1 ) and global clade Ib sequences from GISAID, confirmed all Thai isolates as clade Ib. The genomes showed close relatedness to clade Ib viruses reported internationally, consistent with patients’ travel histories. All isolates exhibited a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region and 52–61 amino acid substitutions compared with the clade Ia reference. Genome sequences were submitted to GISAID and NCBI to support outbreak response and improve understanding of epidemiologic patterns, enabling more effective public health interventions. IMPORTANCE On 14 August 2024, the World Health Organization declared the monkeypox virus outbreak in Africa a public health emergency of international concern following the emergence of clade Ib. One week later, Thailand confirmed the first monkeypox clade Ib case in Asia. Through whole-genome sequencing and phylogenomic analysis of five cases detected between August 2024 and March 2025, we identified a 1,140-bp deletion in the C3L gene region that distinguishes clade Ib from clade Ia. This deletion directly affects the performance of some commercial real-time PCR assays designed for clade Ia, which rely on amplification of the missing genomic region. Our findings highlight important diagnostic limitations that could lead to misinterpretation or reduced sensitivity in routine testing. Beyond confirming regional introduction linked to global spread, this study underscores the critical role of genomic surveillance in ensuring accurate diagnosis, monitoring viral evolution, and strengthening outbreak response as monkeypox continues to expand internationally.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 2024 年 8 月刚果民主共和国出现猴痘病毒 Ib 分支后,由于 传播 的持续传播和国际传播,世界卫生组织宣布该病毒为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件。我们对 2024 年 8 月至 2025 年 3 月期间在泰国发现的第一批 Ib 分支病例进行了特征分析,并评估了它们的系统发育关系。对疑似病例的病变拭子进行全 基因组 测序。系统发育分析,结合来自 GISAID 的进化枝 Ia (DQ011155.1) 和全局进化枝 Ib 序列,确认所有泰国分离株均为进化枝 Ib。基因组 显示与国际报道的 Ib 分支病毒密切相关,与患者的旅行史一致。与进化枝 Ia 参考相比,所有分离株在 C3L 基因区域均表现出 1,140 bp 缺失和 52-61 个氨基酸取代。基因组 序列已提交给 GISAID 和 NCBI,以支持 暴发 响应并提高对流行病学模式的理解,从而实现更有效的公共卫生干预措施。重要性 2024 年 8 月 14 日,世界卫生组织宣布非洲猴痘病毒 暴发 为国际关注的突发公共卫生事件,继出现 Ib 分支后。一周后,泰国确认亚洲首例猴痘分支Ib病例。通过对 2024 年 8 月至 2025 年 3 月期间检测到的 5 个病例进行全 基因组 测序和系统发育分析,我们在 C3L 基因区域中发现了一个 1,140 bp 的缺失,该缺失将分支 Ib 与分支 Ia 区分开来。这种缺失直接影响了一些为进化枝 Ia 设计的商业实时 PCR 检测的性能,这些检测依赖于缺失基因组区域的扩增。我们的研究结果强调了重要的诊断局限性,这些局限性可能导致常规检测中的误解或敏感性降低。除了确认区域引入与全球传播相关之外,这项研究还强调了 基因组监测 在确保准确的 诊断、监测病毒 进化 以及随着猴痘继续在国际上蔓延而加强 暴发 应对方面的关键作用。

papers.title: Comparative pathogenicity study of monkeypox virus Clade Ib and Clade IIb in a rabbit model
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Mpox has emerged as a significant public health concern, spreading across continents with the emergence of new variants. Clade IIb, from the recent global outbreak, and the newly identified Clade Ib have shown changes in transmission dynamics and possibly in severity. We developed a New Zealand White rabbit model of Mpox by using a combination of intradermal and intravenous routes of administration. Following infection, the rabbits developed erythematous papular lesions on the skin, which progressed to crust and scab formation by the second week, ultimately leading to healing and seroconversion. Infection with the Clade Ib and IIb.A.2.1 lineages revealed that both Monkeypox virus (MPXV) variants caused skin and testicular lesions, as well as viral excretion from the nasal cavity, skin, and testicular tissue. However, there were no significant differences in disease severity between the two variants. These findings suggest that this rabbit model could be useful for evaluating countermeasures against MPXV.

papers.title: Meta-analysis of Asymptomatic Monkeypox Virus Prevalence in Nonendemic Regions, 2022–2024
papers.abstract: In this meta-analysis, we performed a literature search for articles relating to asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) detections published worldwide during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024. The primary outcome was to determine the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections. We conducted a random-effects analysis that yielded a final pooled prevalence of 1.0% (95% prediction interval 0.1%–11.2%). Results did not substantially differ by geographic region or study design. Although those findings are reassuring, we did not evaluate infectivity or transmission potential among asymptomatic persons. MPXV continues to circulate globally; the viral dynamics that enable its persistence remain poorly understood and merit further study.

papers.full_text: Disclaimer: Early release articles are not considered as final versions. Any changes will be reflected in the online version in the month the article is officially released. Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Research Meta-analysis of Asymptomatic Monkeypox Virus Prevalence in Nonendemic Regions, 2022–2024 Suggested citation for this article Abstract In this meta-analysis, we performed a literature search for articles relating to asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) detections published worldwide during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024. The primary outcome was to determine the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections. We conducted a random-effects analysis that yielded a final pooled prevalence of 1.0% (95% prediction interval 0.1%–11.2%). Results did not substantially differ by geographic region or study design. Although those findings are reassuring, we did not evaluate infectivity or transmission potential among asymptomatic persons. MPXV continues to circulate globally; the viral dynamics that enable its persistence remain poorly understood and merit further study. Clade IIb of human monkeypox virus (MPXV), which causes mpox, an infectious disease in the same family as smallpox, began spreading globally in 2022 and prompted international public health concern (1). MPXV can be transmitted through close or intimate contact between humans, through infected animals, or through fomites (1). In the United States, most MPXV infections are spread person-to-person through sexual contact, primarily among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) (1). The emergence of the disease in the United States and Europe, where clinical and epidemiologic resources are more abundant than sub-Saharan Africa, has improved our understanding of the clinical manifestations and epidemiologic characteristics of MPXV. It is now understood that MPXV can be transmitted in 1–4 days before a person has onset of symptoms of infection (1). However, whether persons who remain asymptomatic throughout the course of infection can transmit MPXV to others is much less clear. This uncertainty arises partly because persons need to have lesions to be clinically tested for MPXV in the United States. The prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV infection in the ongoing global outbreak also is unknown and could have important implications for public health efforts. A previous systematic review and meta-analysis of the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections estimated a pooled prevalence of 10.2% (95% CI 2.5%–17.9%) but only included reports available through September 2022 (2). Because most studies in that meta-analysis preceded the 2022 global MPXV outbreak and the analysis also included a report from an outbreak that began in a primate sanctuary in Cameroon, the results may not be generalizable to the ongoing outbreak that primarily affects GBMSM (2). The absence of asymptomatic MPXV detections in study populations has been noted in numerous reports (3–8). For example, a retrospective study noted that only 0.2% of patients tested through PCR were asymptomatic. However, that study was conducted in the summer and fall of 2022, the peak of the global outbreak, when transmission was more widespread in the GBMSM community (9). In contrast, 2 studies that assessed the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections among GBMSM in France and Belgium retrospectively screened anorectal, urine, and oropharyngeal samples and found higher prevalences of asymptomatic detections (5.5% in France and 1.3% in Belgium), although a notable methodologic limitation of those studies is that detection of viral genetic material does not necessarily mean that a person is infectious, whereas a negative test result indicates that infectiousness is highly unlikely (10,11). Because overlooking asymptomatic viral infections, if highly prevalent, could hinder disease control and prevention, we assessed the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections worldwide through a meta-analysis of peer-reviewed articles published during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024. Search Strategy and Selection Criteria We searched PubMed for relevant articles by using the search terms (asymptomatic OR non-lesion OR no lesion* OR without lesion* OR without cutaneous lesion* OR undetected OR unrecognized OR proctitis OR undiagnosed OR no symptom*) AND (monkeypox OR mpox OR MPXV OR MPX OR monkey pox OR monkeypox virus OR MPV). Because PubMed contains relevant biomedical literature related to MPXV and because of resource constraints and the substantial overlap between PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase, we opted for using PubMed as our primary database. We found additional relevant articles through citations from screened studies. We limited results to publication dates during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024, to yield results relevant to the ongoing outbreak. Data Extraction and Management The primary outcome was determination of the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections among persons tested for MPXV. We used the Preferred Reporting Standard of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) checklist to evaluate the searched articles (Figure 1). We did not prospectively register the review protocol. The first author began by screening and removing studies whose titles did not indicate asymptomatic MPXV detections; she also briefly reviewed abstracts of excluded articles. She then screened the abstracts for inclusion and exclusion criteria, after which 2 other authors independently reviewed the remaining full-text articles for inclusion. If discordance about whether to include an article occurred, we consulted a third co-author to determine whether the article met eligibility criteria. Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria Studies about asymptomatic MPXV detections published during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024, were eligible for inclusion. We followed the PICO (population, intervention, comparison, outcome) framework to synthesize our research question. We searched for articles that assessed individual adults (population) who tested positive for MPXV by PCR. PCR testing for asymptomatic persons enrolled in those studies was conducted by using pharyngeal, anorectal, urethral swabs, urine, or blood. We compared those asymptomatic persons who tested positive for MPXV to those who tested negative for MPXV (comparison). We used the following inclusion and exclusion criteria and completed the JBI (formerly Joanna Briggs Institute) critical appraisal checklist for prevalence studies to determine whether studies should be included in the meta-analysis. The study must have been conducted during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024; taken place outside of sub-Saharan Africa (in nonendemic regions for MPXV); been primary research (not a review of already published studies); must have had a population of >1 person; been conducted on the individual patient level (e.g., not an ecologic study or a study that does not provide counts of individual characteristics); researched people >18 years of age (e.g., any sex, sexual orientation, or race/ethnicity); researched transmission between humans only; not selectively sampled on MPXV infection (e.g., the study did not only include persons with MPXV); performed PCR testing to determine the presence of MPXV infection; and included persons who displayed no physical symptoms of MPXV as determined by explicitly stating that persons were asymptomatic, undetected, clinically inapparent, did not experience lesions or rashes, or a combination of these descriptions. Any mention of symptomology excluded a person from being asymptomatic or (if it did not otherwise include asymptomatic MPXV) the entire article from inclusion. We initially considered vaccination status as inclusion criteria but ultimately did not include the criteria because very few studies accounted for vaccination status. We then excerpted the following from each included article: author (or authors), study design (cross-sectional, prospective cohort, retrospective cohort, mixed cohort), publication date, study recruitment dates, country where the study participants were recruited, number of asymptomatic MPXV patients in the study population, and total number of persons who were tested for MPXV in the study population. Data Analysis We calculated the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections as the cumulative number of asymptomatic MPXV detections divided by the total number of study participants tested for MPXV. We first constructed a funnel plot of the included research studies and statistically tested for biases and then estimated the pooled effect by using random effects estimates and their associated 95% prediction intervals (PIs) (12). We built logistic regression models to calculate random effects estimates, which assume that included studies estimated different interventional effects that follow an approximately normal distribution, and implemented a continuity correction of 0.5 for studies without any events. Our models used a logit transformation before pooling with the restricted maximum-likelihood estimator for between-study variance. To estimate the 95% PIs, we used the τ statistic that quantifies the variance between effect sizes, which, in this case, was the observed proportion of asymptomatic MPXV detections across studies. We used the 95% PIs to predict the underlying effect that would be seen in a hypothetical study similar to the studies included in the meta-analysis. We conducted sensitivity analyses by using meta-regression to determine whether the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections differed by geographic region or study design. We defined regions by continent and included Asia, Europe, and North America. Study designs included cross-sectional studies, mixed cohorts, prospective cohorts, and retrospective cohorts. If a study could not be grouped into a mutually exclusive category for either of those potential effect modifiers, we excluded it from that specific sensitivity analysis. Finally, we quantitatively assessed between-study heterogeneity using the ι2 test, which measures the percentage of variability between studies that is not attributable to chance (13). We classified heterogeneity as low (<25%), moderate (25%–50%), and high (>50%). We conducted all analyses by using the meta and metafor packages from R version 4.4.1 (The R Project for Statistical Computing, https://www.r-project.org) (14,15). Our search criteria yielded 1,299 articles, of which we excluded 1,250 (96.2%) based on the titles, which did not include information about asymptomatic MPXV or MPXV transmission (Figure 1). We also reviewed the abstracts of those excluded articles to ensure they did not include information about asymptomatic MPXV detections. We screened the abstracts and introductions of the 49 remaining articles and excluded 15 (31%) that did not meet inclusion criteria; 3 (6%) of the excluded articles described individual MPXV patients, and 12 (24%) were not primary studies (i.e., they were descriptive reviews, editorials, or commentaries). We then reviewed the remaining 34 full-text articles and excluded 18 (53%) because they either were ecologic studies (n = 2), did not explicitly study asymptomatic MPXV detections (n = 5), used modeling to project the number of MPXV detections (n = 2), studied a population <18 years of age (n = 1), were a case–control study that selectively sampled on MPXV case status (n = 1), did not provide individual-level characteristics (n = 3), were an already existing meta-analysis that included studies of primate sanctuary workers with MPXV (n = 1), or did not perform PCR testing to determine MPXV infection (n = 3). A total of 16 articles met all inclusion criteria. One author compiled the JBI checklist for all included studies and a second author validated the checklist (Appendix Table). Of the included studies, 8 were prospective cohort studies, 2 were cross-sectional studies, 5 were retrospective cohort studies, and 1 was a mixed cohort study (i.e., containing prospective and retrospective cohorts) (Table 1). Three studies were from the United States, 3 from Belgium, 2 from Germany, and 1 each from Austria, Denmark, England, France, Italy, Japan, Spain, and Switzerland. Of the 16 included studies, 14 reported the number of male participants (Table 1). The study populations ranged in size from 25 in the cross-sectional study by Brosius et al. (17) to 6,600 in the cross-sectional study conducted by Koppe et al. (21). Cumulatively, of 14,511 persons who were tested for MPXV by PCR, 128 persons (weighted by the study’s inverse variance) had asymptomatic MPXV. Results of the Egger’s test to evaluate for publication bias was not statistically significant (p = 0.08), also yielding a symmetric funnel plot. Combined, those findings offered no significant evidence of publication bias having occurred and provided sufficient evidence to proceed with a random-effects analysis (Appendix Figure) (12). The ι2 value was 82.6% (95% CI 72.9%–88.8%), indicating a high level of heterogeneity between studies. The random-effects analysis yielded a final pooled prevalence of 1.0% (95% PI 0.1%–11.2%) (Figure 2). We included all 16 studies in the meta-regression analysis of geographic region and study design. We observed no statistically significant difference in the odds of asymptomatic MPXV detections in Asia (odds ratio [OR] 0.45 [95% CI 0.02–10.03]) and Europe (OR 1.70 [95% CI 0.29–10.05]) compared with the odds in North America. In our assessment of the odds of asymptomatic MPXV detections by study design, we found no significant difference in the odds of MPXV detections in mixed cohorts (OR 0.06 [95% CI 0.00–3.94]), prospective cohorts (0.17 OR [95% CI 0.02– 1.20]), and retrospective cohorts (OR 0.24 [95% CI 0.03–1.83]), all relative to the odds of MPXV detections in cross-sectional studies (Table 2). We assessed the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections during the global outbreak of clade IIb MXV in nonendemic regions that has been ongoing since 2022. We included 16 peer-reviewed studies that encompassed 14,511 adults of both sexes (95.0% of all participants were men), sexual orientations, races, and ethnicities who were tested for MPXV. The pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections in this population was 1%, much lower than the previously reported pooled prevalence of 10% reported in a previous meta-analysis that included a large proportion of cases from Cameroon (where MPXV is endemic). We found that asymptomatic MPXV prevalence did not differ by study design or geographic region. Most of the 16 studies we included were conducted in countries in Europe and were either prospective or retrospective analyses. The prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections in all 16 studies ranged from 0% to 8%; mean prevalence was 1.55%. Studies with larger sample sizes were weighted more heavily in our analysis, which led to a lower pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections. The prospective study conducted by Brosius et al. (17) found the highest prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV among tested persons, probably because they restricted their sample to persons reporting sexual or intimate contact with someone with MPXV, whereas all other studies sampled from sexually active populations (largely those attending sexual health clinics); some, but not all, reported contact with a person with MPXV. The low prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections observed in our study may be, in part, attributable to the increasing number of persons who have been previously infected with or vaccinated against MPXV with modified vaccinia Ankara–Bavarian Nordic vaccine, the latter of which may reduce the risk for infection from 75% to 86% (depending on the number of doses received) and reduces the severity of MPXV disease if the patient is infected (24,25). Because studies have shown that prophylactic vaccination with modified vaccinia Ankara–Bavarian Nordic vaccine reduces the severity of disease, vaccinated persons who become infected with MPXV may experience symptoms that are so mild that they may be classified as asymptomatic (and, especially in the United States, because of the absence of non–lesion-based testing, go undetected) (26,27). Persons who are asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic also may be less likely to seek medical attention, and the most ubiquitous assays to evaluate MPXV in clinical settings require an active lesion to swab for viral testing. However, the studies included in this analysis did not require lesions for testing; detection was assessed through PCR testing of oropharyngeal, rectal, or urethral swab samples or of urine or blood, and most of those studies evaluated high-risk groups (e.g., men at sexual health clinics). One major strength of this meta-analysis was the inclusion of 16 different studies. We found a low pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections among the entire pooled study population; however, that finding may be an underestimate because of underreporting of asymptomatic MPXV. Although the findings are reassuring, because we did not evaluate infectivity or transmission potential among asymptomatic persons, more accurate and widely available diagnostic MPXV testing tools (e.g., oropharyngeal swabs, as recommended by the World Health Organization) would help to better characterize the epidemiology and virology of MPXV from a surveillance standpoint, even if the use of those testing tools would be unlikely to change clinical practice (1,26,28). Another strength of our meta-analysis is the inclusion of studies only relevant to the ongoing MPXV outbreak (i.e., those conducted since the outbreak began in May 2022). Because our analysis excluded studies conducted before the most recent MPXV outbreak began, we can be sure that our findings are a closer representation of the actual proportion of current asymptomatic MPXV infections than the findings from the prior meta-analysis that included studies condu…

Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Research Meta-analysis of Asymptomatic Monkeypox Virus Prevalence in Nonendemic Regions, 2022–2024 Suggested citation for this article Abstract In this meta-analysis, we performed a literature search for articles relating to asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) detections published worldwide during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024. The primary outcome was to determine the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections. We conducted a random-effects analysis that yielded a final pooled prevalence of 1.0% (95% prediction interval 0.1%–11.2%). Results did not substantially differ by geographic region or study design. Although those findings are reassuring, we did not evaluate infectivity or transmission potential among asymptomatic persons. MPXV continues to circulate globally; the viral dynamics that enable its persistence remain poorly understood and merit further study. Clade IIb of human monkeypox virus (MPXV), which causes mpox, an infectious disease in the same family as smallpox, began spreading globally in 2022 and prompted international public health concern (1). MPXV can be transmitted through close or intimate contact between humans, through infected animals, or through fomites (1). In the United States, most MPXV infections are spread person-to-person through sexual contact, primarily among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) (1). The emergence of the disease in the United States and Europe, where clinical and epidemiologic resources are more abundant than sub-Saharan Africa, has improved our understanding of the clinical manifestations and epidemiologic characteristics of MPXV. It is now understood that MPXV can be transmitted in 1–4 days before a person has onset of symptoms of infection (1). However, whether persons who remain asymptomatic throughout the course of infection can transmit MPXV to others is much less clear. This uncertainty arises partly because persons need to have lesions to be clinically tested for MPXV in the United States. The prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV infection in the ongoing global outbreak also is unknown and could have important implications for public health efforts. A previous systematic review and meta-analysis of the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections estimated a pooled prevalence of 10.2% (95% CI 2.5%–17.9%) but only included reports available through September 2022 (2). Because most studies in that meta-analysis preceded the 2022 global MPXV outbreak and the analysis also included a report from an outbreak that began in a primate sanctuary in Cameroon, the results may not be generalizable to the ongoing outbreak that primarily affects GBMSM (2). The absence of asymptomatic MPXV detections in study populations has been noted in numerous reports (3–8). For example, a retrospective study noted that only 0.2% of patients tested through PCR were asymptomatic. However, that study was conducted in the summer and fall of 2022, the peak of the global outbreak, when transmission was more widespread in the GBMSM community (9). In contrast, 2 studies that assessed the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections among GBMSM in France and Belgium retrospectively screened anorectal, urine, and oropharyngeal samples and found higher prevalences of asymptomatic detections (5.5% in France and 1.3% in Belgium), although a notable methodologic limitation of those studies is that detection of viral genetic material does not necessarily mean that a person is infectious, whereas a negative test result indicates that infectiousness is highly unlikely (10,11). Because overlooking asymptomatic viral infections, if highly prevalent, could hinder disease control and prevention, we assessed the prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections worldwide through a meta-analysis of peer-reviewed articles published during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024. Search Strategy and Selection Criteria We searched PubMed for relevant articles by using the search terms (asymptomatic OR non-lesion OR no lesion* OR without lesion* OR without cutaneous lesion* OR undetected OR unrecognized OR proctitis OR undiagnosed OR no symptom*) AND (monkeypox OR mpox OR MPXV OR MPX OR monkey pox OR monkeypox virus OR MPV). Because PubMed contains relevant biomedical literature related to MPXV and because of resource constraints and the substantial overlap between PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase, we opted for using PubMed as our primary database. We found additional relevant articles through citations from screened studies. We limited results to publication dates during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024, to yield results relevant to the ongoing outbreak. Data Extraction and Management The primary outcome was determination of the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV detections among persons tested for MPXV. We used the Preferred Reporting Standard of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) checklist to evaluate the searched articles (Figure 1). We did not prospectively register the review protocol. The first author began by screening and removing studies whose titles did not indicate asymptomatic MPXV detections; she also briefly reviewed abstracts of excluded articles. She then screened the abstracts for inclusion and exclusion criteria, after which 2 other authors independently reviewed the remaining full-text articles for inclusion. If discordance about whether to include an article occurred, we consulted a third co-author to determine whether the article met eligibility criteria. Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria Studies about asymptomatic MPXV detections published during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024, were eligible for inclusion. We followed the PICO (population, intervention, comparison, outcome) framework to synthesize our research question. We searched for articles that assessed individual adults (population) who tested positive for MPXV by PCR. PCR testing for asymptomatic persons enrolled in those studies was conducted by using pharyngeal, anorectal, urethral swabs, urine, or blood. We compared those asymptomatic persons who tested positive for MPXV to those who tested negative for MPXV (comparison). We used the following inclusion and exclusion criteria and completed the JBI (formerly Joanna Briggs Institute) critical appraisal checklist for prevalence studies to determine whether studies should be included in the meta-analysis. The study must have been conducted during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024; taken place outside of sub-Saharan Africa (in nonendemic regions for MPXV); been primary research (not a review of already published studies); must have had a population of >1 person; been conducted on the individual patient level (e.g., not an ecologic study or a study that does not provide counts of individual characteristics); researched people >18 years of age (e.g., any sex, sexual orientation, or race/ethnicity); researched transmission between humans only; not selectively sampled on MPXV infection (e.g., the study did not only include persons with MPXV); performed PCR testing to determine the presence of MPXV infection; and included persons who displayed no physical symptoms of MPXV as determined by explicitly stating that persons were asymptomatic, undetected, clinically inapparent, did not experience lesions or rashes, or a combination of these descriptions. Any mention of symptomology excluded a person from being asymptomatic or (if it did not otherwise include asymptomatic MPXV) the entire article from inclusion. papers.title_original: Meta-analysis of Asymptomatic Monkeypox Virus Prevalence in Nonendemic Regions, 2022–2024

analysis.scope_and_question: This meta-analysis aimed to determine the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) detections in nonendemic regions during May 12, 2022–September 13, 2024. The focus was on MPXV, specifically clade IIb, which causes mpox, an infectious disease related to smallpox.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review included a literature search for articles on asymptomatic MPXV detections published globally during the specified timeframe. A random-effects analysis was conducted to calculate the pooled prevalence, which was 1.0% (95% prediction interval 0.1%–11.2%). The analysis excluded studies that did not meet the criteria for asymptomatic MPXV detection.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled prevalence of asymptomatic MPXV infections was found to be 1.0% (95% prediction interval 0.1%–11.2%). Results did not vary significantly by geographic region or study design, indicating a consistent pattern of asymptomatic MPXV prevalence across nonendemic areas.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is uncertainty regarding whether asymptomatic individuals can transmit MPXV. This is partly due to the reliance on clinical testing methods that require the presence of lesions. Additionally, the study did not assess infectivity or transmission potential among asymptomatic persons.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to understand the viral dynamics that allow MPXV to persist in the population. Specifically, studies should investigate the transmission potential of asymptomatic individuals and the role of asymptomatic infections in the spread of MPXV.

analysis.summary_en: This meta-analysis aimed to determine the pooled prevalence of asymptomatic monkeypox virus (MPXV) infections in nonendemic regions during 2022–2024. A random-effects analysis yielded a pooled prevalence of 1.0% (95% prediction interval 0.1%–11.2%). Results were consistent across geographic regions and study designs, but the study did not assess infectivity or transmission potential among asymptomatic individuals. The findings highlight the need for further research on the role of asymptomatic infections in MPXV transmission and persistence, particularly in populations where the virus is spreading rapidly, such as in the United States and Europe.

papers.title: Monkeypox Virus Surveillance in Wastewater, North Carolina, USA, October 2023–May 2025
papers.abstract: In September 2023, the North Carolina Department of Health and Human Services identified a new case of mpox clade II 5 months after the last previous report. To assess possible unrecognized transmission, nonvariola orthopoxvirus testing was implemented at select wastewater sites. During October 29, 2023-May 2025, a total of 801 samples were collected across 16 treatment plants serving ≈2 million residents. We analyzed wastewater detections (n = 47) and clinical cases (n = 45) using a +17-day window. Overall sensitivity of identifying the presence of >1 temporally aligned mpox case within a sewershed was 10.6% (95% CI 6.5%-16.7%); specificity was 95.1% (95% CI 93.2%-96.5%), positive predictive value was 31.9% (95% CI 20.4%-46.2%), and negative predictive value was 83.2% (95% CI 80.3%-85.7%). Restricting detections above the limit of detection reduced sensitivity but increased specificity. Overall, wastewater surveillance showed low sensitivity but provided complementary awareness for public health response.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of wastewater surveillance for detecting mpox virus in North Carolina from October 2023 to May 2025. The research aimed to address the gap in identifying unrecognized transmission of mpox clade II, as the last reported case had occurred 5 months prior. A total of 801 samples were collected from 16 wastewater treatment plants serving approximately 2 million residents. The analysis compared wastewater detections (n = 47) with clinical cases (n = 45) using a +17-day window. The authors interpreted these findings as demonstrating the potential of wastewater surveillance to support early detection and response efforts, despite its limitations. The study's evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of a defined temporal window and integration of both wastewater and clinical data.

papers.full_text: Article summary AI generated The resurgence of mpox has highlighted significant gaps in traditional disease preparedness and response strategies, necessitating innovative approaches to enhance public health efforts. This scoping review systematically maps the applications of artificial intelligence across the mpox epidemic continuum, revealing promising advancements in diagnostic and predictive tools while identifying critical gaps in data quality, validation, and equity that must be addressed for effective real-world implementation. Abstract Background The 2022–2024 global resurgence of mpox (formerly monkeypox) and the successive declarations of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern have exposed persistent weaknesses in conventional disease preparedness, prediction, prevention, and surveillance. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer scalable tools to strengthen each of these pillars, yet the evidence remains fragmented across diagnostic imaging, epidemiological forecasting, genomic analytics, digital infodemiology, and therapeutic discovery. Objective To systematically map the scope, methods, performance, and translational maturity of AI applications across the mpox epidemic continuum, and to identify research gaps that should guide future preparedness for emerging epidemics. Methods We conducted a scoping review following the PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) framework. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Embase were searched from database inception to the final search date of 30 September 2025. Eligible records were concentrated between 2018 and 2025. After de-duplication and two-stage screening performed by a single reviewer, 48 studies meeting predefined eligibility criteria were charted and synthesized under four thematic domains: diagnosis and detection, prediction and forecasting, surveillance and digital epidemiology, and drug and vaccine discovery. Results Deep-learning image classifiers dominated the diagnostic literature, with reported accuracies and area-under-the-curve values ranging from approximately 0.83 to 0.99 for distinguishing mpox skin lesions from clinical mimics. Time-series and neural-network models (ARIMA, LSTM, GRU, and ensemble sub-epidemic frameworks) produced credible short-term case forecasts, while natural-language-processing pipelines tracked public sentiment and misinformation in near real time. AI-assisted genomic surveillance, wastewater monitoring, and structure-based drug and epitope discovery represented rapidly emerging but less mature domains. Reported performance metrics were author-reported values obtained under heterogeneous datasets and validation protocols, and were not pooled. Across studies, small and imbalanced datasets, limited external validation, and weak clinical integration were recurrently reported by the included primary studies. Conclusions AI shows promise in augmenting mpox preparedness, prediction, prevention, and surveillance, but most tools remain at a proof-of-concept stage. Prospective validation, equitable data governance, explainability, and integration into public-health workflows are prerequisites for real-world impact in future epidemics. 1 Novelty of the study Several earlier reviews have already examined AI for mpox. These include systematic and narrative syntheses that span diagnosis, therapeutics, and epidemiology together. We therefore do not claim to be the first to review this field, and we make no claim of chronological primacy. Instead, the contribution of this scoping review is methodological and structural, and rests on three features. First, it applies an explicit, pre-specified PRISMA-ScR methodology to the full preparedness–prediction–prevention–surveillance continuum, rather than to a single modality such as skin-lesion classification. Second, it introduces a structured translational-maturity mapping. This mapping positions each AI application—from proof-of-concept to prospective validationagainst the methodological limitations reported in the primary studies. Third, it distils these findings into a transferable gap-analysis framework. This framework can be reused to appraise AI readiness for the next emerging or re-emerging pathogen. Together, these features move the synthesis beyond a catalog of tools toward an actionable readiness assessment. 2 Background and literature review Mpox is a zoonotic disease caused by the monkeypox virus (MPXV). MPXV is a double-stranded DNA orthopoxvirus that has historically been endemic to the rainforests of Central and West Africa [1]. The first human case was documented in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 1970. Since then, the global incidence has risen at least ten-fold. The median age at presentation has also shifted, from young children in the 1970s to young adults by the 2010s. This trend is widely attributed to the end of routine smallpox vaccination and the resulting decline in cross-protective immunity [2]. The re-emergence of mpox in Nigeria during 2017–18, after a four-decade hiatus, signaled changing transmission dynamics and foreshadowed a wider international threat [3]. This warning was realized in May 2022. An unprecedented multi-country outbreak, driven by the clade IIb lineage B.1, spread to more than one hundred previously unaffected countries. In response, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) on 23 July 2022 [4, 5]. A landmark international case series of 528 infections across sixteen countries clarified the transmission pattern. In this outbreak, transmission occurred predominantly through sexual networks, and the great majority of cases were among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men [6]. The epidemiological picture evolved further in 2024, when the emergence and rapid spread of the more virulent clade Ib in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighboring states triggered a second PHEIC declaration on 14 August 2024 [7, 8]. Continental analyses documented tens of thousands of clinically diagnosed and laboratory-confirmed cases, with disproportionate pediatric mortality and concerning vertical-transmission outcomes [9]. These successive emergencies underscored that mpox is no longer a geographically confined neglected disease but a recurrent global threat requiring agile, technology-enabled responses [10]. Conventional outbreak control remains indispensable. It relies on syndromic case finding, laboratory polymerase-chain-reaction (PCR) confirmation, contact tracing, and reactive vaccination. However, it is constrained by diagnostic delay, clinical overlap with varicella and other vesicular illnesses, limited laboratory capacity in endemic regions, and the sheer velocity of modern global travel [6, 11]. Against this backdrop, artificial intelligence (AI) and its machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) subfields have been proposed as force multipliers. They may accelerate diagnosis, anticipate epidemic trajectories, optimize prevention, and enhance surveillance [12, 13]. Throughout this review, we organize these applications around four operational pillars of the epidemic response: preparedness, prediction, prevention, and surveillance. We refer to these collectively as the “Four-P” continuum, in which surveillance constitutes the fourth pillar. We use this order consistently in the title, abstract, figures, and all sections that follow. 2.1 AI for diagnosis and detection The most extensively developed application is image-based lesion classification. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and, more recently, vision transformers have been trained to discriminate mpox lesions from those of measles, chickenpox, and healthy skin, frequently achieving high reported accuracy [14, 15]. A widely cited deep convolutional network (MPXV-CNN) was trained on more than 139,000 images. It reported sensitivities of 0.83–0.91 and areas under the curve approaching 0.97. It was also deployed in a patient-facing web application for early self-assessment [16]. Optimization strategies such as the Grey Wolf Optimizer, transfer learning, hybrid architectures, and explainable-AI overlays (Grad-CAM, LIME, SHAP) have been used to improve performance and interpretability [17,18,19,20]. Beyond imaging, data-mining and ensemble approaches have been applied to clinical and demographic features for early case detection [21]. 2.2 AI for prediction and forecasting A second cluster of studies applies AI to anticipate epidemic trajectories. Classical time-series autoregressive integrated moving-average (ARIMA) models were used to forecast daily and cumulative case counts across the most affected countries during 2022 [22]. Neural approaches such as artificial neural networks, long short-term memory (LSTM), and gated recurrent unit (GRU) architectures were subsequently shown to capture nonlinear outbreak dynamics with competitive accuracy [23]. Ensemble sub-epidemic modeling frameworks generated calibrated short-term forecasts with quantified uncertainty at both national and global scales, informing real-time response planning [24]. 2.3 AI for surveillance and digital epidemiology A third domain harnesses unconventional data streams. Natural-language-processing (NLP) pipelines, topic modeling, and sentiment analysis of social-media platforms characterized public perception, emotional response, and the spread of misinformation during the outbreak [25,26,27]. Large-scale Twitter datasets and deep-learning narrative mapping enabled near-real-time infodemic monitoring [28, 29], while AI-augmented genomic surveillance tracked lineage diversification, APOBEC3-mediated mutation signatures, and transmission chains across continents [30,31,32]. An emerging and innovative strand couples automated wastewater virus enrichment with AI models to estimate community case burden, offering a proactive environmental early-warning capability [33]. 2.4 AI for prevention: drug and vaccine discovery A fourth domain applies AI to therapeutics and immunoprophylaxis. AI-driven drug-repurposing and molecular-docking pipelines have nominated candidate inhibitors of MPXV targets, including the identification of clinically used antiretrovirals as broad-spectrum poxvirus inhibitors [34, 35]. Machine-learning epitope-prediction tools and dedicated platforms such as PoxiPred have accelerated rational, structure-based vaccine design against orthopoxviruses [36, 37], and broader frameworks position AI as an integrating layer linking vaccine design, antiviral discovery, and real-world monitoring for emerging viral threats [38]. 2.5 Research gap and objectives Despite this proliferation, the literature remains siloed, with diagnostic, predictive, surveillance, and therapeutic studies seldom appraised together. Existing reviews tend to focus on a single modality, most often skin-lesion classification, and rarely interrogate dataset quality, external validation, equity, or clinical integration across domains [39,40,41]. Few synthesize how these applications collectively map onto the operational pillars of epidemic response. This scoping review addresses that gap with the following objectives: (i) to map the breadth of AI/ML applications across mpox preparedness, prediction, prevention, and surveillance; (ii) to summarize the data sources, model families, and reported performance within each domain; (iii) to describe recurrent methodological limitations and translational barriers reported in the primary studies; and (iv) to articulate a research and policy agenda for AI-enabled preparedness against future emerging epidemics. 3 Methods 3.1 Study design This study was designed as a scoping review, an approach suited to mapping a heterogeneous and rapidly evolving evidence base and to identifying knowledge gaps rather than appraising the effect of a single intervention. The review was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and was guided methodologically by the Arksey and O’Malley framework as refined by Levac and colleagues. A protocol defining the research question, eligibility criteria, search strategy, and charting approach was defined a priori before screening commenced. A completed PRISMA-ScR checklist is provided as Supplementary File 2. 3.2 Study selection process Five electronic databases: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Embase were searched from database inception to the final search date of 30 September 2025, supplemented by Google Scholar, citation chaining of included studies, and curated preprint servers. The search combined controlled vocabulary (Medical Subject Headings, MeSH) and free-text title/abstract terms across two concept blocks joined with Boolean operators. For PubMed, the full strategy was: (“mpox”[tiab] OR “monkeypox”[tiab] OR “MPXV”[tiab] OR “Monkeypox virus”[MeSH]) AND (“artificial intelligence”[tiab] OR “machine learning”[tiab] OR “deep learning”[tiab] OR “neural network*”[tiab] OR “natural language processing”[tiab] OR “forecasting”[tiab] OR “Artificial Intelligence”[MeSH] OR “Machine Learning”[MeSH]). The complete, copy-pasteable search strings for all five databases, together with the number of records retrieved from each, are provided in Supplementary File 1. Records were eligible if they were peer-reviewed primary studies or clearly labeled preprints that applied an AI, ML, or DL method to an mpox-related preparedness, prediction, prevention, diagnosis, or surveillance task, were published between database inception and the search date (with eligible records concentrated between 2018 and 2025), and were written in English. Editorials, commentaries without primary analysis, non-mpox studies, and reports lacking any extractable AI component or outcome were excluded. Titles and abstracts were screened by a single reviewer, who then assessed the full texts of potentially eligible records against the eligibility criteria. Because screening was performed by a single reviewer, no inter-reviewer agreement statistic (such as Cohen’s kappa) was calculated; this is acknowledged as a limitation. Uncertain inclusions were resolved by re-examining the full text against the predefined eligibility criteria. The selection process is summarized in the PRISMA flow diagram (Fig. 1). 3.3 Data extraction and data curation A structured data-charting form was piloted on five studies and refined iteratively. For each included study we extracted bibliographic details (authors, year, country), the thematic domain, the AI/ML technique family, the data source and sample size, the validation strategy and the highest validation level reported (internal hold-out, cross-validation, external validation, or prospective), the geographic origin of the training and validation data, the principal performance metric, and the authors’ stated limitations. Charting was performed by a single reviewer, who re-checked all extracted entries against the source publications to minimize transcription error. Extracted data were curated in a structured spreadsheet, with categorical harmonization of technique families (deep learning, classical ML, time-series/statistical, NLP, and generative/structure-based AI) to enable consistent cross-study comparison. No attempt was made to impute missing values; where metrics were not reported, the field was recorded as not available. A strict no-fabrication policy was applied throughout: only data explicitly reported in the source publications were charted. 3.4 Statistical tests and statistical analysis Consistent with scoping-review methodology, the primary synthesis was descriptive and narrative rather than meta-analytic, because the included studies were methodologically heterogeneous in task, data, and outcome definition, precluding valid pooling. Quantitative charting outputs were summarized using frequencies and proportions, and visualized as temporal and thematic distributions (Fig. 2). Where studies reported comparable diagnostic metrics (accuracy and area under the curve) or forecasting error metrics (mean absolute percentage error), these were tabulated and displayed descriptively to illustrate the range of reported performance (Fig. 4). These displays are unweighted, author-reported values and are not the result of pooled statistical estimation; they must not be pooled or compared directly across studies. No new inferential statistical tests were performed on the charted data. Where primary studies reported p-values, the original authors’ significance thresholds are noted descriptively. In keeping with scoping-review methodology, no formal critical appraisal or risk-of-bias assessment of the included studies was undertaken; accordingly, observations regarding dataset quality, external validation, and other methodological limitations reflect issues reported by the primary study authors rather than conclusions drawn from a structured quality appraisal. 4 Results The search identified 1,380 records, of which 48 studies met the eligibility criteria after de-duplication and two-stage screening (Fig. 1). The included studies clustered into four thematic domains: diagnosis and detection (n = 17), prediction and forecasting (n = 13), surveillance and digital epidemiology (n = 10), and drug and vaccine discovery (n = 8). Publication activity was concentrated after the 2022 outbreak, reflecting the field’s reactive emergence (Fig. 2A). A conceptual framework summarizing how these domains map onto the mpox epidemic continuum is presented in Fig. 3. 4.1 Diagnosis and detection Seventeen studies addressed automated detection, overwhelmingly through image classification of skin lesions. Deep CNN architectures, including ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, EfficientNet, MobileNet, and Inception variants and hybrid or transformer-based models were the dominant approaches [14,15,16,17,18,19, 42]. papers.title: COGNITIVE-BEHAVIORAL ASPECTS OF STUDENTS’ KNOWLEDGE, ATTITUDES, AND PRACTICES TOWARD MONKEYPOX: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
papers.abstract: Background: Monkeypox (mpox) has infected 103,048 people and caused 229 deaths from January 2022 to July 2024. Approximately 83.6% of cases were associated with sexual activity, highlighting the important role of behavioral factors in disease transmission. Inadequate knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among students may contribute to misinformation and suboptimal preventive behaviors, particularly among students in health-related disciplines who become future healthcare professionals. Purpose: This systematic review aimed to identify the levels and factors associated with KAP regarding mpox among students. Methods: A comprehensive literature search through ScienceDirect, Scopus, and PubMed up to September 2024 using predefined keywords and Boolean operators. Eligible articles were screened according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The quality of the included studies was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklist. Results: Of 44 articles identified across three databases, six studies met the inclusion criteria. Three of six studies reported good knowledge, three of five reported positive attitudes, and one of two studies reported good practices. Educational, information-related, and demographic factors were associated with KAP. Conclusion: Students’ KAP toward mpox varied across settings, with knowledge ranging from poor to good, generally favorable attitudes, and limited evidence on preventive practices. These findings support the integration of emerging infectious diseases into relevant curricula and improved access to reliable health information among students.

papers.title: Analysis of Mpox intervention measures in presence of environmental transmission pathway using data from DRC
papers.abstract: This paper develops a mathematical model for Mpox transmission dynamics accounting for disease transmission through interpersonal contact as well as from microbes infested environment. The endemic equilibrium of the model was evaluated for two cases. (1) When it is assumed that the microbes in the environment play no role in the spread of the disease, and it was shown that the endemic equilibrium is unique, exists when R 0 is greater than unity, and is globally asymptotically stable. (2) For the case when environmental microbes concentration plays a role in disease transmission, the model was shown to possibly exhibit backward bifurcation at R 0 . This indicates that lowering R 0 below 1 may not eliminate Mpox when the disease is already endemic, due to the stable endemic equilibrium. Numerical results, based on outbreak data from the DRC indicate that; (1) increased interpersonal contact has the potential of making the disease worse, (2) high isolation rate and accelerated recovery of infected individuals through any possible intervention can easily contain the disease. The results further show that environmental contamination does not substantially influence disease transmission rates. More still, it is observed that implementation of influential mitigation measures results in lower and delayed peaks of the number of infected. This is essential for healthcare systems to prepare for more emergency cases and isolation facilities when needed most especially in under resourced communities or countries. Our findings highlight the need for comprehensive interventions addressing both behavioural and environmental factors, especially in environments with limited resources.

papers.title_zh: 在DRC数据支持下分析猴痘干预措施在存在环境传播途径中的情况
papers.source_body_en: This paper develops a mathematical model for Mpox transmission dynamics accounting for disease transmission through interpersonal contact as well as from microbes infested environment. The endemic equilibrium of the model was evaluated for two cases. (1) When it is assumed that the microbes in the environment play no role in the spread of the disease, and it was shown that the endemic equilibrium is unique, exists when R 0 is greater than unity, and is globally asymptotically stable. (2) For the case when environmental microbes concentration plays a role in disease transmission, the model was shown to possibly exhibit backward bifurcation at R 0 . This indicates that lowering R 0 below 1 may not eliminate Mpox when the disease is already endemic, due to the stable endemic equilibrium. Numerical results, based on outbreak data from the DRC indicate that; (1) increased interpersonal contact has the potential of making the disease worse, (2) high isolation rate and accelerated recovery of infected individuals through any possible intervention can easily contain the disease. The results further show that environmental contamination does not substantially influence disease transmission rates. More still, it is observed that implementation of influential mitigation measures results in lower and delayed peaks of the number of infected. This is essential for healthcare systems to prepare for more emergency cases and isolation facilities when needed most especially in under resourced communities or countries. Our findings highlight the need for comprehensive interventions addressing both behavioural and environmental factors, especially in environments with limited resources.
papers.abstract_zh: 本文开发了一个 猴痘 传播 动态数学模型,用于解释通过人际接触以及微生物感染环境产生的疾病 传播。对两个病例的模型的地方性平衡进行了评估。(1) 假设环境中的微生物对疾病的传播没有作用,并且证明地方病平衡是唯一的,当R 0 大于1时存在,并且全局渐近稳定。(2) 对于环境微生物浓度在疾病传播中起作用的情况,模型被证明可能在R 0 处表现出向后分岔。这表明,当疾病已经流行时,由于稳定​​的流行平衡,将 R 0 降低到 1 以下可能无法消除 猴痘。基于 DRC 的 暴发 数据的数值结果表明: (1)人际接触增加有可能使疾病恶化,(2)高隔离率和感染个体的加速康复通过任何可能的干预可以轻松遏制疾病。结果进一步表明,环境污染并没有显着影响疾病 传播 的发病率。更重要的是,据观察,实施有影响力的缓解措施会导致感染人数的峰值降低和延迟。这对于医疗保健系统在最需要时为更多紧急情况和隔离设施做好准备至关重要,特别是在资源匮乏的社区或国家。我们的研究结果强调需要针对行为和环境因素采取综合干预措施,特别是在资源有限的环境中。

papers.title: High-content image-based screening reveals vaccinia virus membrane proteins as potential regulators of LC3 lipidation.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Autophagy is a catabolic process used for the degradation of organelles and proteins, and it also functions as a cellular defense mechanism, known as xenophagy, during infection. Vaccinia virus (VACV), the prototypic poxvirus, replicates exclusively in the cytoplasm of host cells. It is known that VACV infection causes LC3 lipidation while preventing autophagosome formation, yet the viral protein(s) responsible have not been identified. Using infection time-course Western blotting and a phospholipase D band-shift assay, we show that VACV drives genuine LC3-II formation, rather than a block in pro-LC3 cleavage, and that this depends on early viral gene expression. To identify the gene(s) involved, we generated a dsRed-LC3-I-GFP reporter cell line and developed an image-based screening approach based on single-cell LC3 granularity, which we applied to 80 early VACV genes. The screen revealed that VACV-induced lipidation is regulated in both directions. Follow-up validation identified H3 as a negative regulator and the membrane proteins A14, L5, and G5 as positive contributors to LC3 lipidation. These findings provide the first systematic map of VACV genes affecting LC3 lipidation and suggest that the interplay between VACV and autophagy is more directed than previously thought. IMPORTANCE: Poxviruses, including vaccinia virus and the closely related monkeypox virus, remain a significant public health concern and are increasingly exploited as vaccine and cancer immunotherapy vectors. Understanding how these viruses manipulate host defenses is therefore important for both antiviral and biotechnology applications. Autophagy is a key cellular defense pathway, and vaccinia virus is known to trigger lipidation of the autophagy protein LC3 while blocking productive autophagy, although the viral genes driving this remained unknown. Using an image-based screening strategy, we identify several early vaccinia virus genes that increase or decrease LC3 lipidation, showing that the virus actively regulates this process in both directions. These findings reveal a more targeted interaction between vaccinia virus and host autophagy than previously recognized and provide a broadly applicable screening approach for studying virus-autophagy interactions.

papers.title: Municipality size and epidemiological characteristics among confirmed mpox cases in Spain
papers.abstract: In 2022, a multistate mpox outbreak represented a new global health challenge and highlighted sexual contact as the main route of transmission. Spain reported the highest number of cases in Europe but showed an irregular distribution of cases across its territory. This study aims to describe the characteristics of mpox cases among individuals living in large cities versus smaller municipalities, and to examine whether municipality size is associated with mpox incidence and with epidemiological and clinical characteristics among confirmed cases. This is a cross‐sectional study of mpox cases in men aged ≥ 16 years confirmed between June 2022 and January 2023 in seven Spanish regions. Epidemiological and clinical variables were analysed in large cities (population ≥ 200 000) and smaller municipalities. Descriptive analyses were performed. Odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI95%) were obtained through logistic regression models to describe characteristics of mpox cases among individuals. To assess differences in cumulative incidence according to municipality size, cumulative incidence ratios (aCIR CI95%) were obtained through Poisson regression models with robust variance. Among the 1,162 reported mpox cases, 776 (66.8%) were from large urban areas. Among mpox cases, living in large cities was significantly associated with being born in low-income countries (aOR = 2.1, 1.2–3.5), having a previous sexually transmitted infection (STI) (aOR = 1.6, 1.1–2.3), participating in chemsex (aOR = 1.7, 1.0–2.7), having sex in private leisure venues (aOR = 1.5, 1.1–2.2), using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) (aOR = 1.7, 1.1–2.5), and regularly using condoms during casual sex (aOR = 1.9, 1.3–2.9). Clinical complications were less frequent in large cities (aOR = 0.4, 0.2–0.7). Living in a large city was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of mpox (aCIR = 2.7; 1.9–3.7) compared with living in smaller municipalities. Living in a large city was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of mpox. It was also associated with characteristics linked to chemsex practices, sexual encounters in private leisure venues and previous STI diagnosis. These findings support considering municipality size and urban social dynamics when planning public health responses to mpox.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 2022 年,多州 猴痘 暴发 代表了新的全球健康挑战,并强调性接触是 传播 的主要途径。西班牙报告的病例数是欧洲最多的,但其境内病例分布不规则。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项针对 2022 年 6 月至 2023 年 1 月期间在西班牙七个地区确诊的 16 岁以上男性 猴痘 病例的横断面研究。该研究旨在描述居住在大城市与小城市的个体中 猴痘 病例的特征,并研究城市规模是否与 猴痘 发病率 以及确诊病例的流行病学和临床特征相关。
elements_zh.methods: 对大城市(人口≥ 200,000)和较小城市的流行病学和临床变量进行了分析。通过逻辑回归模型获得具有 95% 置信区间 (CI95%) 的比值比 (aOR),以描述个体中 猴痘 病例的特征。为了根据城市规模评估累积 发病率 的差异,通过具有稳健方差的泊松回归模型获得累积 发病率 比率 (aCIR CI95%)。
elements_zh.main_results: Among the 1,162 reported mpox cases, 776 (66.8%) were from large urban areas. Living in a large city was significantly associated with being born in low-income countries (aOR = 2.1, 1.2–3.5), having a previous sexually transmitted infection (STI) (aOR = 1.6, 1.1–2.3), participating in chemsex (aOR = 1.7, 1.0–2.7), having sex in private leisure venues (aOR = 1.5, 1.1–2.2), using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) (aOR = 1.7, 1.1–2.5), and regularly using condoms during casual sex (aOR = 1.9, 1.3–2.9). Clinical complications were less frequent in large cities (aOR = 0.4, 0.2–0.7). Living in a large city was associated with a higher cumulative incidence of mpox (aCIR = 2.7; 1.9–3.7) compared with living in smaller municipalities.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现支持在规划 猴痘 的公共卫生应对措施时考虑城市规模和城市社会动态。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 进行了描述性分析。它还与化学性行为、私人休闲场所的性接触以及之前的性传播感染 诊断 相关的特征有关。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,未建立因果关系。样本量足以进行描述性分析,但可能不足以用于更复杂的统计模型。该研究并未控制所有潜在的混杂因素,研究结果的普遍性可能仅限于所研究的地区和人群。

papers.title: In Vitro Selection and Characterization of Tecovirimat-resistant Mpox Virus.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox virus (MPXV) is the causative agent of mpox, a disease characterized by skin lesions, and remains a global threat since the recent 2022 outbreak. Tecovirimat is an antiviral agent that inhibits MPXV replication in vitro and in vivo by targeting the viral phospholipase VP37 protein and blocking viral envelope wrapping. Although tecovirimat has been administered to many mpox patients, the emergence of tecovirimat-resistant MPXVs carrying mutations in the VP37 protein has been reported, particularly in immunocompromised individuals. However, the impact of these respective mutations on drug susceptibility and viral fitness have not been fully characterized. METHODS: Tecovirimat was applied as a selective pressure in vitro to isolate MPXV variants carrying clinically observed VP37 substitutions. Drug susceptibility among the major VP37 mutations was compared, and the cellular fitness of the isolated viruses was evaluated. RESULTS: The VP37-N267D and -Y258C mutants showed markedly reduced susceptibility to tecovirimat compared with the VP37-I372N and -T245I (+I7L-A388S) mutants, while retaining susceptibility to an alternative anti-MPXV agent, brincidofovir. The VP37-I372N, T245I (+I7L-A388S), Y258C, and N267D mutants exhibited viral fitness comparable to that of the parental virus in A549 and Vero cells, as well as in MRC-5 and HaCaT cells. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide insights into the phenotype of each VP37 mutation and emphasize the importance of developing antivirals with distinct mechanisms of action to effectively combat tecovirimat-resistant MPXV.
